Personally I have lived in almost every state for a time and in both the city and rural America. I was born abroad and learned and lived the first few years of my life in another country. If you want food there are literally tons of options and something is always open somewhere in the city. With that type of convenience people are much more prone to building routines that are not sustainable and are dependent on the network of busy work they have absorbed themselves into. In rural America we grow the food we eat and know where it comes from before we send it to the markets. We see our neighbors daily for coffee at the local McDonald's as our form of convenience prior to going back out to the fields or mines or back to the station. The concentrations of people in the city may have a large say in how our nation is percieved but that's not America. Out here where I live we stand for the National Anthem because we know the real America and what it stands for and we stand for each other. The ideals our founders fought for are the same ideals We fight to protect and preserve. We provide the life so many take for granted and when things get bad we will be the ones that absorb the impact and help get this country moving again, like always. If you want a taste of the real America leave the city and go to a small community or rural town and talk to real Americans.
